beats.text: That's not what I sound like.
If you cringe at your own recorded voice, you're far from alone.
When you speak, you hear yourself twice.
Once through the air, like everyone else.
And once through your own skull.
Your head boosts the low frequencies. So to you, your voice sounds deeper and fuller.
A recording only catches the air. That's the voice everyone else hears.
In a 2013 study, people rated a set of voices. Hidden among them was their own.
Most didn't recognise it. And they rated it higher than other listeners did.
So it's not your voice. It's the surprise.

sources: Hullar, T. E., in Scientific American: bone-conducted sound reaches the cochlea through the head; the head enhances lower-frequency vibrations; a recording keeps only the air-conducted part.

Hughes, S. M. & Harrison, M. A. (2013). I like my voice better: Self-enhancement bias in perceptions of voice attractiveness. Perception 42(9), 941-949. 80 participants; own voice included unknowingly; rated more attractive than other raters rated it.
